Content:
One way to simplify a determinant calculation is to create a row (or column) containing all zeros except for one entry. Then, we can use a Laplace expansion across that row (or column) to compute the determinant.

Content:
Let's demonstrate this method on the matrix [MATH: A] below.

Content:
[MATH: [2|1|1; 1|2|3; 8|14|17]]

Content:
Notice that we can make entries to the right of [MATH: a_{21}=1] equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Content:
Since adding a multiple of one column to another column in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

Content:
[MATH: =|2|1|1; 1|2|3; 8|14|17||C_{2}:=C_{2} + (− 2)C_{1}; C_{3}:=C_{3} + (− 3)C_{1}; =|2|− 3|− 5; 1|0|0; 8|− 2|− 7|.]

Content:
Expanding the result along the [MATH: 2]nd row, we get

Content:
[MATH: =|2|− 3|− 5; 1|0|0; 8|− 2|− 7|; = 1 ⋅ (− 1)^{2 + 1}|− 3|− 5; − 2|− 7|; = − (21 − 10); = − 11.]

sections.normalized_html:
Let's make entries below [MATH: a_{11}=1] equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (or column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

[MATH: =|1|2|3|1; 2|− 1|5|− 7; 4|− 2|4|− 5; − 3|3|− 3|− 4||R_{2}:=R_{2} + (− 2)R_{1}; R_{3}:=R_{3} + (− 4)R_{1}; R_{4}:=R_{4} + 3R_{1}; =|1|2|3|1; 0|− 5|− 1|− 9; 0|− 10|− 8|− 9; 0|9|6|− 1|.]

Expanding the result along the [MATH: 1]st column, we get

[MATH: =|1|2|3|1; 0|− 5|− 1|− 9; 0|− 10|− 8|− 9; 0|9|6|− 1|; = 1 ⋅ (− 1)^{1 + 1}|− 5|− 1|− 9; − 10|− 8|− 9; 9|6|− 1|; =|− 5|− 1|− 9; − 10|− 8|− 9; 9|6|− 1|.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
One way to simplify a determinant calculation is to create a row (or column) containing all zeros except for one entry. Then, we can use a Laplace expansion across that row (or column) to compute the determinant.

Content:
